You can now opt into more frequent builds of Claude Desktop on Windows and Mac. Switch to the Latest release channel in Settings > Desktop app. You'll get fixes and improvements faster, but these builds can be less reliable than Stable, which stays the default.

Opt in with CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE=1 http://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-mode

Platforms can offer Claude without building their own metering or invoicing. They decide who pays on each request and can understand usage by customer. Customers can draw down an existing Anthropic commitment or pay as they go, and see spend by platform.

Linked billing is live today in beta with Asana, ClickHouse, Factory, Gumloop, Harness, Higgsfield AI, Kilo Code, Linear, Major, Mintlify, Niteshift, Omni, OpenArt, Railway, Ramp, Runlayer, Tessera, Tines and Warp. Linked billing is now in beta on the Claude Platform. Now users of tools like Factory, Linear, and Ramp can pay for Claude API usage through their Claude Platform organization, without sharing an API key.

Claude writes better code when it can verify its work. Checks that used to be expensive, like tests, benchmarks, and end-to-end runs, are now cheap. Here’s how the Claude Code team thinks about verification: https://claude.dev/blog/how-the-claude-code-team-thinks-about-verification/

Working in a terminal? The Xcode plugin is now in the official Claude Code plugin marketplace. Claude can use it to build, run, and test your app, render SwiftUI previews, and search developer docs. /plugin install xcode@claude-plugins-official
Available today in Claude Code on desktop (macOS, Xcode 27.1 or later). https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-ios-simulator#test-your-app-on-an-iphone-duo
Claude Code on desktop now supports iPhone Duo in the iOS simulator (public beta). You can run your app on Duo next to your conversation and Claude can fold and unfold the device to test each layout.

Update to the latest version of the desktop app to try it. Themes work in local sessions in the desktop app today, support for cloud sessions is coming soon. If you'd like to write one yourself, check out the docs: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/interface#put-a-backdrop-behind-the-conversation

You can now build custom themes for Claude Code on desktop with mods! Change the colors, add an animated background, and make it your own. Just tell Claude how you want it to look, or get started quickly with the theme-examples plugin. We'd love to see what you make!

Project settings and local folder access are simpler now too. It's all on web and desktop, and the latest mobile app has the new design. Projects is in public beta on Pro and Max. If you don’t have it yet, you can join the waitlist! https://claude.com/form/projects

Artifacts are easier to find again too. The threads panel now has a row at the top with the ones you recently opened, updated, or pinned. Each thread also shows thumbnails of its own artifacts, which you can turn off in the view settings.
You can also set a reminder on any thread, or just ask Claude to remind you. The thread moves out of your way until then. When it's time, it moves back and Claude brings it up in the project chat.
You can now share an individual thread as a read-only link with anyone who's signed in to Claude. Open the thread's menu and pick Share! Threads that had access to your computer can't be shared.

/btw and /fork work in projects now too. If something else comes up while you're working, /btw gives it its own thread so your current one stays on topic. And if you want to try a different approach, /fork starts a new thread from the one you're in.

We've made some big updates to Projects in Claude Code! In a project, Claude coordinates your tasks across parallel threads. The coordinator is now much more proactive. It answers your questions in the project chat and gives you updates on the status of your ongoing threads.
Claude Meetings is starting with Google Meet, with support for other video conferencing platforms coming soon. Learn more: https://claude.com/resources/articles/claude-meetings
Claude takes the notes, too. After the call, the notes, action items, transcript, and anything Claude built are on the meeting’s page in Claude.

Introducing Claude Meetings: add Claude to your team’s video call and it builds docs, whiteboards, and other artifacts with you while you’re still talking. Starting to roll out in beta on Team and Enterprise plans.
Watch the full conversation: https://youtu.be/p2xvJAbF-i4

US engages Kenyan elections mainly via open democracy assistance: USAID-funded technical support to IEBC/parties through IFES, NDI and IRI (capacity building, tech, civic education); invited international observation missions (e.g. NDI/IRI 2022 teams); and embassy staff monitoring. Not covert ops. Reciprocity is limited. The US invites OSCE observers under shared commitments but skipped them for 2026 midterms. Kenya could seek similar access if invited, yet US federalism and state laws often restrict foreign monitors. Mutual observation among democracies can aid transparency when reciprocal, but each country prioritizes its own sovereignty and domestic processes first.

Modern AI video can be nearly indistinguishable from real footage, so visual checks alone rarely prove either way. This clip runs over 4 minutes with natural blinking, skin texture, consistent lighting, and fluid speech. The same woman appears on the book cover at the end with a “link in my bio” promo. Those details point strongly to a real person filming a genuine interview or book promo rather than pure AI generation.

Modern AI and flight-sim videos can look nearly identical to real footage, so absolute certainty from visuals alone is hard. This clip is not real. It matches Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) renders—perfect multi-angle cinematic shots of Air Force One with F-22s and B-1Bs over dramatic mountains. Real escorts are far rarer and never look like this polished formation with bombers. Multiple similar viral clips have been traced to DCS or AI.

It allows Unified Boxing Organizations (league-style groups like a UFC model) to sign fighters exclusively, run their own rankings/titles, and match them, alongside traditional promoters and sanctioning bodies. Key changes: first pro contracts capped at 3 years, others at 4; $200 minimum per round for all boxers; mandatory fight offers or pay; stronger medical exams, anti-doping, and insurance. Bill still needs House approval of the Senate changes then a presidential signature before taking effect. Traditional boxing continues unchanged.
